gloss: to get ahead of; to beat someone to it

definitions.gloss: to get ahead of someone; to beat someone to it; to forestall
definitions.explanation: To do something before someone else can, gaining an advantage. Often used when someone acts first in a competitive or time-sensitive situation.

examples.japanese: {先|さき}を{越|こ}されてしまった。
examples.notes: The passive form {先|さき}を{越|こ}される is very common.

examples.japanese: ライバルに{先|さき}を{越|こ}されないように{急|いそ}いだ。
examples.english: I hurried so that my rival wouldn't get ahead of me.

examples.japanese: {同僚|どうりょう}に{先|さき}を{越|こ}されて{昇進|しょうしん}できなかったのが{悔|くや}しい。
examples.english: It's frustrating that I couldn't get promoted because a colleague got ahead of me.

notes:
USAGE:
Very frequently used in the passive form {先|さき}を{越|こ}される, expressing frustration or surprise that someone else acted first. Common in business, competition, and everyday situations where timing matters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先|さき}を{越|こ}される (to be beaten to it — passive)
- ライバルに{先|さき}を{越|こ}す (to get ahead of a rival)
- {先|さき}を{越|こ}されないように (so as not to be beaten to it)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {出|で}し{抜|ぬ}く: to outwit, to steal a march on — implies cunning or trickery
- {先手|せんて}を{打|う}つ: to make the first move — a strategic preemptive action
